summary: Cerebras sells AI inference and training systems built on its own wafer-scale chip. Revenue comes from hardware sales (CS-4 systems, S8) and from a cloud service that rents the capacity back out. FY2025 revenue was $510M, up 75.7% from $290M (C:revenue_growth@FY2025), and the top two customers made up 86% of FY2025 revenue (F48). In Q2 2026, GAAP revenue was $180.1M and core revenue was $209.9M, up 103% (S29). Gross margin is split: core is 41% and GAAP is 14% (F50, F51), and the cause of the gap is not documented. The remaining performance obligations of $25.4B (F52) and the 600MW of contracted data center capacity (F53) show large future demand. They also show a shift toward a capital-heavy cloud model, with a $420M quarterly capex figure (F62). Unit economics cannot be assessed because CAC, churn and cohort data are missing. Customer concentration is the main weakness in the business.

moat.point: The wafer-scale chip architecture and the CS-4 launch are positioned as the fastest AI inference (S8, S15). The sources are Cerebras's own announcements and press coverage. No third-party benchmarks, share data or price-retention records are in the evidence.

Contracted data center capacity of 600MW (F53) and a $25.4B backlog (S24) suggest scale, and management says core gross margin is moving toward the 60% range in 2027 (S29). That target is a company statement and has not been shown in results. Core gross margin of 41% in Q2 is above the Q3 guidance of 38~40% (F57), so the near-term trend is flat to slightly down.

The partnerships with AMD (disaggregated inference) and Gimlet Labs show ecosystem expansion (S18, S16). No record of retention, repurchase or price increases at the customer level was found, so switching costs are unproven.

findings.point: The top two customers accounted for 86% of FY2025 revenue (F48), and the S-1 reporting links them to G42 and MBZUAI. Revenue depends on very few counterparties. The concentration may have eased in 2026, but the evidence does not show this.

Core gross margin was 41% (F50) against GAAP gross margin of 14% (F51) in Q2 2026. FY2025 gross margin was 39% (F47). The gap between core and GAAP margin has not been explained. Core excludes items that GAAP includes, and the filing needs to be read to see which ones. Core margin of 41% is not clearly higher than the FY2025 level of 39%.

Q3 guidance calls for core revenue of $214~216M and core gross margin of 38~40% (F56, F57). The consensus of $211.9M before guidance (F59) is slightly below that. Core margin is guided below the 41% reported in Q2, so there is no sign yet of margin expansion.

Q2 GAAP revenue of $180.1M missed the consensus of $194M (F58). Hardware was weak and cloud beat estimates (S30). The stock fell 14~16% after the report (S9, S20). This suggests the market is giving less weight to the hardware business and more to cloud, but the cloud and hardware split is not in the facts.

RPO is $25.4B (F52), and deferred revenue is only $170M (F12, 1.7억). The backlog is recognized over a long period, and the timing, customer mix and termination terms are not known. OpenAI and AWS contract sizes are also not found. The backlog is therefore a signal of demand and cannot be used as a forecast of revenue.

Cash was $6.74B at the end of Q2 (F3, 67.4억) and equity was $9.15B (F16, 91.5억), both well above the Q1 levels of $1.72B (F2) and -$190M (F15). The increase follows the May IPO. Q2 capex was $420M (F62) and operating cash flow was -$59.82M (F64). Building out the cloud capacity is funded by IPO money for now.

The competitors are NVIDIA and AMD, but no share data or competitor margin comparison was collected. Management says 2026 core revenue will be $880~890M, raised from $855~865M (S29). The market position cannot be judged from the evidence, which holds only company guidance and press coverage.
